title: linear_to_srgb branches at the FORWARD threshold (0.04045) instead of the inverse threshold (0.0031308) in both the palcheck oracle and the derivation script — the CVD simulation is mathematically wrong and discontinuous
detail: The inverse sRGB map must branch at linear 0.0031308, not 0.04045. At c=0.04045 it returns 0.523 where truth is 0.222 — a downward jump. In-band channels are mismeasured (deutan lane_best_effort blue: 131 vs true 56), so quoted distances aren't the claimed model.
recommended_fix: Branch at c <= 0.0031308 in both copies (palcheck.odin, derive_a11y_palettes.py); re-derive all pair distances, re-tune any pair that fails under the corrected simulation, and update the PR's quoted min-dists.

title: Parity settings twin never models row activation its own comments claim ('the row-adjust'); the touch leg's claimed 'activates it' step does not exist
detail: The twin implements focus only; no row-adjust mutation exists, and the touch script has no activate step. The press-seam activation path (the B2 cycle_scale surface a touch-only player uses) is never exercised or asserted — parity green certifies less than claimed.
recommended_fix: Mirror activation in the twin (a row tap steps the row's value, as the app does per B2) and assert the stepped end-value on every device; or correct both comments to claim focus-only equivalence.

title: Spec Design Notes say reduced-motion pins a mid-envelope factor (0.99); the PR body and a11y_reduced demo pin full static width
evidence:
spec-7-3-accessibility-core.md (Design Notes):
- Reduced-motion static value: a fixed mid-envelope factor (e.g. 0.99) — deterministic, golden-stable; packet motion/lane speeds stay (gameplay readouts, not effects).

_pr_body.md:
- **Reduced-motion pins the pulse to full static width** (max legibility, deterministic + golden-stable), not an average — a constant ring reads better than a frozen mid-pulse.

demos/a11y_reduced.dem:
# a11y_reduced.dem — Story 7.3: the juice scene with REDUCED MOTION: the
# PULSE16 ring + crisis-outline swell pin static at full width (pulse_read).
detail: Two documents added by this same PR state opposite reduced-motion semantics (mid-envelope 0.99 vs full static width); the spec text was never reconciled with the shipped choice.
recommended_fix: Update the spec Design Note to 'static full width via pulse_read', matching the implementation and the PR's documented rationale.

title: Intent inventory contradicts itself: spec Code Map lists 4 intents (Settings_Toggle, Panel_Navigate, Panel_Activate, Scale_Step); PR body lists 3 differently-named ones
evidence:
spec-7-3-accessibility-core.md (Code Map):
- `app/input/types.odin` + `poll/controller/touch` -- new Intents (Settings_Toggle, Panel_Navigate, Panel_Activate, Scale_Step); mapped on all devices

_pr_body.md:
- **Input parity by construction**: new intents (`Toggle_Settings`, `Settings_Navigate`, `Settings_Activate`) mapped across keyboard (S, arrows, Enter, Esc), controller (Y, D-pad, A, B), and touch (chip + row taps via the shared ui-press seam).
detail: Same PR, two incompatible intent inventories: four vs three, names reversed (Settings_Toggle vs Toggle_Settings), Scale_Step present only in the spec. One list is stale.
recommended_fix: Reconcile both lists against the actual app/input/types.odin enum and delete the stale inventory (including whether Scale_Step exists).

title: Spec Code Map advertises an `a11y <mode>[,<mode>]` combined-mode demo verb; the implemented parser accepts exactly one directive and no demo combines modes
detail: The Code Map promises comma-combined modes (e.g. palette+reduced — the real colorblind-and-motion-sensitive player); the parser takes one subcommand and would reject 'deutan,reduced'. No golden captures a combined mode.
recommended_fix: Either implement comma-combination in the a11y directive plus a combined demo/golden, or correct the Code Map to the single-directive verb actually shipped.

  4. Where a pair collides, search the mode-space remap: shift lightness
     (the axis that survives ALL three deficiencies) and nudge hue onto the
     deficiency's residual discriminable axis (blue-yellow for deutan/protan,
     red-green for tritan), within the light-canvas aesthetic (muted tones,
     warm reserved for danger).

def scale_lum(rgb, target_l):   # no call site anywhere in the script

def verify(mode, remap, classes, tune=True):
    """Check every pair under the simulation on EFFECTIVE colors. Returns the
    (possibly empty) failure list — no silent auto-nudging: anchors are the
    canon; if a pair fails, HAND-TUNE the anchors above."""
